CS2-H-01.note: "peculiar enough to account for the restriction WITHOUT HELP" is the whole item: a range that needs nothing further said is self-explanatory. "Anomalous" is the trap for a solver who transfers 'peculiar' from the soil to the range, but the botanists found the range explained, not puzzling.

CS2-H-02.note: I disagree with the key. The blank is syntactically pinned by "and the manuscripts ENCOURAGE THE DESCRIPTION: whole passages are struck through, and the replacements are entered in a hurried hand" - the description the manuscripts encourage is 'impulsive', not 'calculated'. Under the key that clause is simply false, and the 'Yet' has to reach back and overwrite a description the sentence has just said the evidence supports. The explanation concedes impulsive is 'the reading the hurried hand invites' without noticing that the text asserts that reading rather than merely inviting it. Fix by changing the connective (e.g. 'have been called impulsive, and the manuscripts encourage the description ... Yet ___') or by demoting it to 'the manuscripts seem to bear the description out'.

CS2-H-03.note: Deciding span: "blocks that held policies were paced out and checked twice a year, while blocks that held none were sketched from the end of the street" - detail present in some blocks, absent in others. Nothing says the maps lie (A) or that the sketched blocks cannot be checked (C); D imports decay the text never mentions.

CS2-H-04.note: The charge must be (i) testable against the appendix and (ii) DIFFERENT from the reinterpretation, or "better read as" is vacuous. "every table in the appendix reproduces what the authors say it does" tests fidelity, i.e. misreporting. 'Overstates' is the strong distractor - it is exactly what the summary paragraph does - and is ruled out only by that second feature, which is what makes this legitimately hard.

CS2-H-05.note: "accept material from any donor and set no ceiling" = no discrimination; the correction is that the staff "reject about half", i.e. they do discriminate. But 'exhaustive' is genuinely defensible: 'no ceiling on how many samples of one variety' is a completeness claim, and 'two thirds from four research stations' is precisely the narrowing of coverage that defeats exhaustiveness. Both halves of the second sentence are live, one for each candidate; the item does not clearly signal which is load-bearing.

CS2-H-06.note: Deciding span: "a fact that the defense had ALREADY CONCEDED IN WRITING BEFORE THE TERM OPENED". Cross-examining a witness to a fact you have already granted buys nothing, so the silence is efficient. B self-destructs on 'already' - a concession on the record cannot be made again by staying quiet.

CS2-H-07.note: 'render' takes the first clause: "a reader can follow the disagreement from session to session" = traceable. 'Unintelligible' is the mirror built out of the second clause ('never learns why') and is the best-constructed distractor in the words-in-context set, because the sentence deliberately gives each candidate its own clause; the tie is broken by 'render' governing what the minutes DO record.

CS2-H-08.note: "reads as faint praise UNTIL ONE NOTICES WHAT IT EXCLUDES" is an instruction to pick a word that sounds flat but is not: "differed from itself by less than the modern specification allows" is self-consistency = uniform, and the foundry sentence supplies the reason that was hard. 'Unremarkable' and 'serviceable' are the faint-praise decoys and both die on the forty-point sampling result, which is remarkable. Best-built item in the batch.

CS2-H-09.note: Sentence 2 makes elevation the variable; sentence 3 sorts by it ("the LOWEST sites lose more than half"). A is the strongest wrong answer but misnames the target of the qualification - the cores do not touch the burial RATE, only retention. D fails because the last sentence explicitly does not resolve anything ("its fate has not been traced").

CS2-H-10.note: "each of the eleven PROVED to have taken water from the pump by a route he had not anticipated" - the counterexamples dissolved. B is the mirror and is killed by the same clause; the item is a one-clause decision, which is why it is medium rather than hard.

CS2-H-11.note: The closing sentence hands the answer over verbatim: "nothing has been found wrong with the reasoning that produced the old account". A inverts it, B invents two explanations, C invents a prediction. Whole-structure items with a summary final sentence are not hard.

CS2-H-12.note: Sentence 2 is "granted the charge and declined to act on it"; sentences 3-4 are the reason for declining. B reverses the outcome (she did not revise), C describes sentence 1, D inverts the order.

CS2-H-13.note: "Neither definition is wrong, and the two figures are not in competition" is a consequence drawn from sentence 3's finding. A is the real trap - it converts a positive finding (both correct, of different things) into an unresolved verdict (undeterminable). D fails because the closing sentence extends the cost rather than disputing it.

CS2-H-14.note: "Nothing about a hummingbird's flight is settled by the size of its wings" clears out the expected variable so the shoulder joint can be named. A misassigns what the film established (the joint, not the wing claim); B calls the opener a concession when it is the thesis.

CS2-H-15.note: Four-part structure maps one-to-one onto the four sentences (table / does not compose / reprinted eighty years / likeliest explanation). A invents harm, C invents a second rejected explanation, D says it defends the table against inaccuracy when the text grants the inaccuracy.

CS2-H-16.note: "between eleven and nineteen percent, a range wide enough that the growth reported in two of the last five years falls inside it" - quantify, then show it swamps the reported signal. Labelled hard but is not: all three distractors describe OTHER sentences (B = sentence 2's mechanism, A and D = sentence 4), so 'is this even about sentence 3' clears the item without engaging the function.

CS2-H-17.note: Text 2 runs two prongs and C is the only option naming both: "those are also the hospitals with the fewest vacancies" (selection) and "a unit held by one nurse for twelve hours has fewer witnesses" (recording artifact). A's fatigue claim appears nowhere in Text 2; D turns an argument into a policy proposal.

CS2-H-18.note: "turns up again at forty to sixty centimeters, below where the corers stop" - the surface figure is not the field's figure. C is the mirror (claims destruction rather than relocation) and is contradicted by "Plowing does not destroy carbon; it moves it".

CS2-H-19.note: Deciding span: "A policy that helps chiefly the unaffiliated newcomer is worth having. It is not the policy the journals believe they have adopted, which is one that treats every submission alike." - real effect, unevenly delivered. C contradicts Text 1's 'vanishes when dropped'; B is a denial Text 2 never makes.

CS2-H-20.note: "the range across the structure settles well below the range measured in the open channel" plus "the shortfall is largest where the channel is narrowest", which is aimed at the narrows specifically. But this is guessable with no passage at all: A is an engineering worry, B restates Text 1's own arithmetic as if it were an objection, D is a recommendation - C is the only option shaped like a rebuttal. Labelled hard; it is the weakest distractor set in the cross-text group.

CS2-H-21.note: "not at all in two reaches where elk numbers fell just as sharply but no dams were built" is the controlled comparison, handed over almost verbatim. B is the one option that would help Text 1 rather than answer it.

CS2-H-22.note: "an evenly spread error rate on held-out material tells you nothing about the error it will make here" - the record is granted and its reach denied. D is the overreach trap: Text 2 argues the figure is uninformative, which is not evidence for the opposite conclusion. C contradicts Text 2's own concession that the features are legible.

CS2-H-23.note: "Print circulation counts a renewal as a fresh loan; the e-book platform does not" plus the 3-to-1 worked example: the two series are not commensurable, so 'total up, print flat' supports nothing. A and D both accept the comparison Text 2 refuses.

CS2-H-24.note: "nothing in the design separates what the parents transmitted from what the site supplied" is the closing sentence of Text 2 restated. Like CS2-H-20 it is answerable with no passage: A is a flat denial of an obvious fact, B a specific prediction, C a recommendation - only D is a critique of inference.
